properties.displayName: gatehouse - MCP tool definition changed after approval (rug pull)
properties.description:
A tool's definition (description, schema or annotations) no longer matches the pin
that was approved for it, and gatehouse removed the tool from the agent's view. A
changed description is the classic MCP "rug pull": a server that was trusted when it was
installed starts shipping instructions to the model later. Triage: run `gatehouse diff`
against the server and compare ChangedFields. Re-approve legitimate upgrades with
`gatehouse pin`.
properties.query:
GatehouseEvents_CL
| where EventType == "detection" and DetectorId == "listing.pin_mismatch"
| extend PinnedSha256 = tostring(Details.PinnedSha256),
         CurrentSha256 = tostring(Details.CurrentSha256)
| mv-expand ChangedField = Details.ChangedFields to typeof(string)
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            Occurrences = dcount(EventId), Sessions = dcount(AgentSessionId),
            ChangedFields = make_set(ChangedField, 10), PinnedSha256 = take_any(PinnedSha256)
    by Host, ServerName, UpstreamName, ToolName, CurrentSha256

alertDetailsOverride.alertDisplayNameFormat: MCP rug pull: {{ServerName}}/{{ToolName}} changed after approval

properties.displayName: gatehouse - Unapproved MCP tool offered or invoked
properties.description:
Either an MCP server offered a tool that was never approved (strict pinning, or a tool
added after the server was first trusted), or the agent tried to call a tool it was
never shown (unlisted, filtered or stale). Calls to hidden tools point to a hidden
capability or to a model steered by injected instructions. One row per session, server
and tool.
properties.query:
GatehouseEvents_CL
| where (EventType == "detection" and DetectorId == "listing.unpinned")
    or (EventType == "tool.call" and Action == "blocked"
        and DecisionBasis in ("unlisted_tool", "stale_tool_list"))
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            TimesOffered = countif(EventType == "detection"),
            BlockedCalls = countif(EventType == "tool.call"),
            Rules = make_set(RuleId, 5), Risk = take_any(ToolRisk)
    by Host, AgentSessionId, ServerName, ToolName

properties.displayName: gatehouse - Credential sent to an egress or exec MCP tool
properties.description:
A credential (cloud key, token, private key, connection string, and so on) was found in
the arguments of a tool that can send data out or run code. The Action column shows
whether gatehouse blocked it, which depends on the policy. The secret itself is never
logged: MatchSummary is masked and MatchFingerprint is an HMAC, so the same leaked
secret can be tracked across sessions without being disclosed. Triage: if Action is not
blocked, rotate the credential.
properties.query:
GatehouseEvents_CL
| where EventType == "detection" and DetectorId == "args.secrets"
| where ToolRisk in ("egress", "exec")
| extend Fingerprint = tostring(Details.MatchFingerprint)
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            Attempts = count(), Actions = make_set(Action, 5),
            Locations = make_set(Location, 10), Masked = take_any(MatchSummary)
    by Host, AgentSessionId, ServerName, ToolName, ToolRisk, RuleId, Fingerprint

properties.displayName: gatehouse - Guardrail tampering or telemetry loss
properties.description:
Something tried to weaken gatehouse itself or the SOC's visibility into it. Any of
these fires the rule:
- policy.tampered: the policy file changed on disk during a session.
- policy.load_failed: the policy failed to load, so gatehouse blocks every call.
- args.self_protect: an agent tool call referenced gatehouse's own policy, pins, key or
  logs.
- gatehouse.fail_open: telemetry was lost (the one fail-open path in ADR-0001).
An agent editing its own guardrails maps to Impair Defenses.
properties.query:
GatehouseEvents_CL
| where EventType in ("policy.tampered", "policy.load_failed", "gatehouse.fail_open")
    or (EventType == "detection" and DetectorId == "args.self_protect")
| extend Signal = iff(EventType == "detection", DetectorId, EventType)
| project TimeGenerated, Host, AgentSessionId, ServerName, Signal, Severity, Action,
          Reason, ToolName, Location, PolicySha256

properties.displayName: gatehouse - Burst of blocked MCP tool calls in one agent session
properties.description:
Ten or more tool calls from the same agent session were blocked within five minutes.
A single block is routine. A burst means the agent keeps retrying something the policy
forbids, usually because injected instructions are steering it or because it is
probing for hidden tools. AgentSessionId groups all gatehouse wrappers under one agent
process, so the count spans servers.
properties.query:
let threshold = 10;
GatehouseEvents_CL
| where EventType == "tool.call" and Action in ("blocked", "denied", "approval_required")
| summarize BlockedCalls = count(), Servers = make_set(ServerName, 10),
            Tools = make_set(ToolName, 20), Reasons = make_set(DecisionBasis, 10),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            Host = take_any(Host)
    by AgentSessionId, Window = bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where BlockedCalls >= threshold

alertDetailsOverride.alertDisplayNameFormat: {{BlockedCalls}} blocked MCP tool calls in one agent session

properties.displayName: gatehouse - Prompt injection followed by egress on another MCP server
properties.description:
A tool result on one MCP server contained a prompt-injection or exfiltration-beacon
finding, and within 10 minutes the same agent session called an egress or exec tool on
a *different* server. Each gatehouse wrapper sees one server, so neither event alone
shows the attack chain; AgentSessionId joins them. The injected result may have been
withheld (Action = blocked) and the agent still acted, for example because the same
content reached it another way, or the policy only logs findings. Triage: read the
injection finding's MatchSummary and RuleId, then check what the egress call sent
(ArgsHmac lets you match it against other sessions without seeing the arguments).
properties.query:
let window = 10m;
let injections = GatehouseEvents_CL
    | where EventType == "detection" and Direction == "server_to_client"
    | where DetectorId in ("response.injection", "response.exfil_url")
    | summarize InjectionTime = min(TimeGenerated), InjectionRules = make_set(RuleId, 10),
                InjectionAction = take_any(Action), InjectionSummary = take_any(MatchSummary)
        by AgentSessionId, Host, SourceServer = ServerName, SourceTool = ToolName;
let egress = GatehouseEvents_CL
    | where EventType == "tool.call" and ToolRisk in ("egress", "exec")
    | project EgressTime = TimeGenerated, AgentSessionId, EgressServer = ServerName,
              EgressTool = ToolName, EgressRisk = ToolRisk, EgressAction = Action, ArgsHmac;
injections
| join kind=inner egress on AgentSessionId
| where EgressServer != SourceServer
| where EgressTime between (InjectionTime .. (InjectionTime + window))
| summarize FirstEgress = min(EgressTime), EgressCalls = count(),
            EgressTools = make_set(strcat(EgressServer, "/", EgressTool), 10),
            EgressActions = make_set(EgressAction, 5)
    by AgentSessionId, Host, SourceServer, SourceTool, InjectionTime,
       tostring(InjectionRules), InjectionAction, InjectionSummary

alertDetailsOverride.alertDisplayNameFormat: Injection from {{SourceServer}}/{{SourceTool}} followed by egress on another server

properties.displayName: gatehouse - Agent session completed the Rule-of-Two trifecta without approval
properties.description:
An agent session that had read untrusted input and private data made a call that
changes state or sends data out (the Rule of Two, ADR-0005), and no human approved it.
Either gatehouse blocked it (flow.mode enforce, or a declined approval), or, in
monitor mode, the call went through. This is the shape of a prompt-injection
exfiltration chain whatever the injection said, so it fires even when no content
detector did. Sessions where the user approved the call are left to the
rule_of_two_by_principal hunting query.
properties.query:
GatehouseEvents_CL
| where EventType == "flow.rule_of_two" and Action != "approved"
| extend FlowMode = tostring(Details.FlowMode),
         SessionLabels = tostring(Details.SessionLabels),
         ToolLabels = tostring(Details.ToolLabels)
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            Calls = count(), Actions = make_set(Action, 5),
            Tools = make_set(strcat(ServerName, "/", ToolName), 10),
            FlowMode = take_any(FlowMode), SessionLabels = take_any(SessionLabels),
            Host = take_any(Host)
    by AgentSessionId

alertDetailsOverride.alertDisplayNameFormat: Rule of Two: an MCP agent session tried to send data out after reading untrusted input and private data

properties.displayName: gatehouse - Private data copied into an outbound MCP tool call
properties.description:
The arguments of an egress call contain text, or a secret, that the same agent
session read from a tool labelled private_data. They may be copied as is, or as
base64, hex or URL-encoded copies (provenance fingerprints, D-043). The source tools
are named in MatchSummary; no data is in the event. Calls the user approved are
excluded. A paraphrase is not caught by this rule, but GH007 still catches it.
properties.query:
GatehouseEvents_CL
| where EventType == "flow.provenance_match"
| where RuleId in ("private-data-copied", "private-secret-copied") and Action != "approved"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            Attempts = count(), Actions = make_set(Action, 5),
            Sources = make_set(MatchSummary, 5), Severity = take_any(Severity)
    by Host, AgentSessionId, ServerName, ToolName, RuleId

properties.displayName: gatehouse - A response control engaged (kill switch, circuit breaker, remote signal)
properties.description:
A response control engaged on a gatehouse host (ADR-0006, D-055). It is one of:
- the kill switch: every MCP tool call on the machine is blocked;
- the circuit breaker: an agent session was locked after repeated high findings;
- a remote control signal, from the Sentinel playbook through the control queue,
  which was applied or dropped.

Each one stops work on the machine until a human acts. Either an attack was
contained and needs follow-up, or someone is using the controls to deny service.
The first engaged event per process is reported; release events are not.
properties.query:
GatehouseEvents_CL
| where (EventType == "control.kill_switch" and tostring(Details.State) == "engaged")
    or EventType == "control.circuit_breaker"
    or (EventType == "control.signal" and tostring(Details.Outcome) in ("applied", "dropped"))
| extend Control = case(
      EventType == "control.signal", strcat("remote ", tostring(Details.SignalAction)),
      EventType == "control.kill_switch", "kill switch",
      "circuit breaker"),
    Incident = tostring(Details.Incident),
    Strikes = toint(Details.Strikes)
| project TimeGenerated, Host, AgentSessionId, ServerName, Control, Severity, Action,
          Reason, Incident, Strikes

properties.displayName: gatehouse - Model-based classifier flagged prompt injection, or failed closed
properties.description:
This fires on two kinds of classifier.verdict event (ADR-0007):
- a classifier in alert or enforce mode scored a tool result or tool definition as
  prompt injection;
- an enforce-mode classifier gave no answer within its budget, so gatehouse withheld
  the content (fail closed).

Shadow-mode verdicts are excluded: shadow is for measuring a model before trusting
it. A hit often means an injection that no regex rule matched (a paraphrase or a
translation). Unavailability means detections are being withheld and users are
being blocked until the model is back.
properties.query:
GatehouseEvents_CL
| where EventType == "classifier.verdict" and tostring(Details.Mode) != "shadow"
| where RuleId == "prompt-injection" or Action == "fail_closed"
| extend Mode = tostring(Details.Mode), Kind = tostring(Details.Kind),
         Score = todouble(Details.Score)
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            Hits = countif(RuleId == "prompt-injection"),
            Unavailable = countif(RuleId == "classifier-unavailable"),
            MaxScore = max(Score), Modes = make_set(Mode, 3), Kind = take_any(Kind)
    by Host, AgentSessionId, ServerName, ToolName, Classifier = DetectorId

properties.displayName: gatehouse - Burst of refused bearer tokens at an MCP endpoint
properties.description:
Ten or more requests from one client address were refused by `gatehouse serve
--oidc-issuer` within five minutes (ADR-0008). The tokens were missing, forged,
expired, for another audience, or lacking a required role. One expired token is
routine. A burst is token spraying, a stolen token being replayed after expiry, or
a client configured against the wrong tenant. Behind a reverse proxy, ClientAddress
is the proxy's address.
properties.query:
let threshold = 10;
GatehouseEvents_CL
| where EventType == "auth.denied"
| extend ClientAddress = tostring(Details.ClientAddress), Error = tostring(Details.Error)
| summarize Failures = count(), Errors = make_set(Error, 5), Reasons = make_set(Reason, 10),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
    by Host, ServerName, ClientAddress, Window = bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Failures >= threshold
